The Advocate For The Petitioner Praying That This
Honble Court May Be Pleased To Quash The Complaint
And Fir Registered In Cr.No.170/2017 By The
Respondent Police Pending On The File Of The 45th
Acmm, Nrupatunga Road, Bangalore For The Offences
Punishable Under Section 498A,506 Read With 34 Of Ipc
And Section 3,4 Of D.P Act Vide Annexure-A And B
Respectively, Etc.
 This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. This petition is filed by the husband, brother-in-law and mother-in-law of the second respondent challenging the proceedings initiated under section 498A and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The complaint was lodged making several allegations, on 01.05.2017, on the basis of which a crime was registered.

It is not in dispute that thereafter the husband and wife filed a petition seeking for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent by filing a petition in M.C. No.83/2018 under Section J.H. Shankarananda vs State Of Karnataka on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49500633/
2 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 on 25.07.2018.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that M.C. No.83/2018 was, however, dismissed for non-prosecution.

He also points out that subsequently the wife initiated proceedings under Section 13(1)(1a)(1b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking for dissolution of the marriage in M.C.
No.141/2018 and the said proceedings has also ended in a decree in favor of the husband.

He specifically points out to the fact that in the petition the wife makes a categorical statement that the husband and wife have not been cohabitating since January 2017 and therefore, the entire premise on which the complaint was lodged that an incident occurred on 15.03.2017 would be unacceptable.
NC: 2024:KHC:20398 4.

In view of the fact that the wife categorically states in her petition filed for divorce that she and her husband were not cohabitating since January 2017, it is obvious that the entire assertions made in the complaint cannot be accepted.

It is also to be noticed here that both husband and wife had filed a petition seeking for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent and subsequently the marriage has in fact been dissolved by grant of a decree.
5. In the light of the above, I see no justification of conducting the proceedings against the petitioners and the proceedings are, therefore, quashed.
6. In view of disposal of main petition, pending I.A. does not survive for consideration and is accordingly disposed of.

Sd/-
